# Home contents claim

Escape of water, Meanwood house, August 2024. Contents policy with Direct Line, policy DL-HC-2093371. Claim reference **HCX-40917**. Writing everything down because the loss adjuster's questions were very specific and I want the timeline straight if anything gets disputed.

## What happened

Sat 10 Aug 2024, about 07:40. Theo came downstairs saying the kitchen ceiling was "crying". The compression nut under the bathroom basin had worked loose and water had been dripping into the void for, we think, days. Brown stain about 80 cm across, light fitting full of water.

- Turned off the stopcock (under the kitchen sink, behind the bleach)
- Electrics off at the consumer unit for the kitchen circuit
- Photos and a 2-minute video before moving anything
- Rang the 24h line 08:15, ref given then: HCX-40917

The basin fix itself (new washer, olive, 15 mm compression fitting) is in [[Leaky tap washer]]. That part isn't covered, it's maintenance.

## Policy details that mattered

- Contents sum insured: £55,000. Unspecified single item limit £2,000
- Excess: £100 standard, but **£350 for escape of water**. I'd never noticed the separate figure
- Accidental damage cover: yes (added 2023, £38 a year extra)
- New for old on everything except clothing and linen
- The ceiling and plaster are **buildings**, not contents. Buildings is a separate policy with Halifax (HBX-7716302) with its own £250 escape of water excess. Two claims, two excesses, £600 out of pocket before a penny back. Furious for about an hour.

## Damaged items, as submitted

| Item | Bought | Paid | Claimed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kenwood Chef KVC3100 mixer | 2019 | £279 | £299 (current model) |
| Wool rug, 160 × 230, Dunelm | 2021 | £189 | £209 |
| Cookbooks, about 30 | various | | £410 |
| Kitchen ceiling light, Habitat | 2020 | £85 | (buildings) |
| Theo's school iPad case + charger | 2023 | £64 | £64 |
| Bread maker, Panasonic SD-YR2550 | 2022 | £169 | £179 |

Total contents claimed: £1,161.

## Loss adjuster visit

Crawford & Co, adjuster Gemma Whitfield, 22 Aug 2024. Took 50 minutes. Questions she asked:

1. When did I last see any damp in the ceiling? (Never.)
2. Had the bathroom been refitted? (2018, previous owners.)
3. Any previous water claims? (No.)
4. Receipts. I had receipts for 4 of the 6 items. For the cookbooks she accepted a list with ISBNs and current prices from Waterstones.

She said the cookbooks were "generously valued" and reduced them to £280. Didn't argue, wasn't worth it.

## Settlement

- Contents agreed: £1,031
- Less £350 escape of water excess
- **Paid: £681**, by BACS on 19 Sept 2024
- Mixer and bread maker replaced via Direct Line's supplier (Hughes) as vouchers instead, which would have been £40 more. Took the cash.

Buildings side: Halifax paid £1,140 for ceiling repair and redecoration minus £250 = £890. Plasterer (Kevin Ashworth) did it 2 Oct.

## Did it affect the premium?

Renewal in March 2025: £214.60, up from £186. Partly the claim, partly everybody's premiums went up. The claim stays on the record for 5 years.

## Lessons

- Read the excess table, not just the headline excess
- Keep receipts in one email folder: `Receipts/Home`. Now done for everything over £100
- A water claim at home is not the same animal as one at the rented flat; who owns what differs completely. See [[Landlord insurance]] for that side.
- Out-of-pocket amounts came from the [[Emergency fund]]. Related: [[Flood insurance]].
